sources.name: Lena Cross
sources.quote: To be honest, I'm not really sure what you're referring to with 'fading fame.' I've just been living my life, working on my craft, and being a mom to Max. I haven't really noticed any change in how people treat me around here on Piedmont Ave. I still run into familiar faces, like Darrin Davis, and we chat about the A's. Sure, I was named in some coverage recently, but it wasn't exactly kind. Still, it's just part of life, you know? I try not to let it get to me.

sources.name: Rowan Pierce
sources.quote: To be honest, I don't really know Lena Cross or follow her work closely. I see the Oakland Alternative Response Initiative getting a lot of attention around here, and I lent a tool to a neighbor recently, but Lena Cross isn't someone I've noticed around Piedmont Ave lately. I'm not sure how I feel about her fading fame because I'm not really aware of her current status.

sources.name: Marin Tao
sources.quote: To be honest, I haven't really thought about Lena Cross or Piedmont Ave that much. I'm pretty focused on my own music scene here in Chinatown. I've noticed some new faces around, probably from the Winter Lights festival, but I don't really know what's going on elsewhere.

sources.name: Rico Valez
sources.quote: To be honest, I haven't really noticed much about Lena Cross's fading fame around Piedmont Ave. I live in Fruitvale, and while I catch the vibe of the city, I don't spend a lot of time over there. I do know that the cultural scene in Oakland is buzzing, and people are excited about what's happening here. I've been feeling that energy, especially with Marin Tao's rise to fame. It's cool to see people taking notice of our city's arts scene.
